note: Long single-chat recall set for D90 (tree.rs tests). One long chat whose early turns hold facts, followed by many turns on other work, then a recent fact. After a session compaction only the recent tail is still in the model's window; the walk must bring the early facts back when asked in that same chat, and must not pack what the window still holds. `t` is minutes before 'now'; gaps over 30 minutes split episodes.

leaves.text: Let's plan the launch. First some context: my daughter's name is Mira and I am off on Wednesday afternoons for her swim class, so no meetings then.
Noted: Mira's swim class keeps Wednesday afternoons free of meetings.
The Stripe key lives in the env var STRIPE_LIVE_2026 on the relay host. Never print it.
Understood. STRIPE_LIVE_2026 holds the Stripe key; I will reference the variable, never its value.
Launch budget is $4,200 total, and our deploy window is Tuesdays 10:00 to 12:00 UTC.
Budget $4,200; deploys on Tuesdays between 10:00 and 12:00 UTC.
Also, the crash from yesterday: the bug was in parser.rs line 212, an off-by-one in the header loop. It is fixed on main.
Recorded: parser.rs line 212, off-by-one in the header loop, fixed on main.
Now the landing page copy. Draft a headline for the hero section.
Headline: "Your agent, always on." Subline: "Arbos runs your work while you sleep and reports back in plain words."
Shorter subline please, and no sleep metaphor.
Subline: "Arbos does the work and reports back in plain words."
Good. Three bullet points for the features section.
1. Runs in its own sandbox. 2. Remembers every chat. 3. Talks like a colleague, not a console.
Swap bullet two for something about tools.
2. Uses the browser, the shell and your files on its own.
Design review notes: the chat header is too tall on Mac, the sidebar icons are mixed weights, the composer border is one pixel off.
Three items filed: header height, icon weights, composer border.
Add a fourth: the unread dot should be the accent colour.
Added: unread dot in the accent colour.
Which of the four is quickest?
The composer border: one constant in the stylesheet.
Let's talk pricing tiers. Free, Pro, Team. Pro at $20 a month.
Free: one agent. Pro $20: five agents, priority models. Team: per seat, shared agents.
Team at $15 a seat with a five-seat minimum.
Team: $15 per seat, minimum five seats ($75 a month floor).
Write the FAQ answer for 'can I cancel any time?'
Yes. Cancel from Settings at any time; access continues to the end of the paid period.
Onboarding flow: sign in with GitHub, pick a name for the agent, say hello. Anything missing?
A one-line explanation of what the sandbox is, before the first message.
Draft that line.
"Your agent gets its own computer. Everything it does happens there, not on yours."
Perfect.
Added to the onboarding copy.
Status page: which checks should it show?
Relay health, model proxy latency, sandbox host capacity, and the last deploy time.
Add TestFlight build number.
Added: current TestFlight build.
New item: the nightly CSV import job. Let's name it ledger-sync and run it at 03:00 UTC.
The CSV import job is ledger-sync, scheduled 03:00 UTC.
It should skip rows with an empty amount column.
ledger-sync will skip rows whose amount column is empty.
And log the count of skipped rows.
It will log how many rows it skipped on each run.
Reminder: the office wifi password changes on the first of each month.
Noted: wifi password rotates on the 1st.
